attribution_limitations: Table 1 prints no unit for the baseline, minimal or maximum CRT cells or for the day-count cells; micrometres appear in the text only for the study-level mean CRT values and on the figure axes.

The daily SD-OCT evaluations are stated as a protocol for 30 consecutive days, while the Results give a series mean of 27.8 examinations and the Methods exclude patients who missed 10 percent of the examinations; the number of examinations for this patient is not stated.

Table 1 prints Maximum CRT lower than Baseline CRT with the day of maximal CRT listed as 1; the table does not say whether the baseline measurement is excluded from the maximum or how days are counted.
The Discussion or figure caption identifies this patient only as patient 8; it is linked to Table 1 row 8 by the shared patient number.

Figure 2 plots the lowest point of the line for patient 8 at about 390 near day 28, close to the minimal CRT 397 on day 29 printed in Table 1; the difference is within chart-reading uncertainty and the table cells are kept.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

The daily SD-OCT evaluations are stated as a protocol for 30 consecutive days, while the Results give a series mean of 27.8 examinations and the Methods exclude patients who missed 10 percent of the examinations; the number of examinations for this patient is not stated.

Table 1 prints Maximum CRT equal to Baseline CRT while listing the day of maximal CRT as 1 and the first day of CRT reduction also as 1; the table does not say whether the baseline measurement is included in the maximum or how days are counted.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

The daily SD-OCT evaluations are stated as a protocol for 30 consecutive days, while the Results give a series mean of 27.8 examinations and the Methods exclude patients who missed 10 percent of the examinations; the number of examinations for this patient is not stated.

Table 1 prints Maximum CRT lower than Baseline CRT with the day of maximal CRT listed as 1; the table does not say whether the baseline measurement is excluded from the maximum or how days are counted.

Figure 2 plots the line for patient 6 lowest at about 705 near day 14 and highest after injection at about 820 near day 27, whereas Table 1 prints minimal CRT 729 on day 15 and maximum CRT 787 on day 1; the column definitions are not stated and the difference is not reconciled.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.

limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

Table 1 does not define the first day of CRT reduction, day of minimal CRT, day of maximal CRT or Maximum CRT columns; for several patients Maximum CRT equals or is below Baseline CRT while the day of maximal CRT is 1 or equals the first day of CRT reduction. All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
Figure 4 plots the day-17 mean bar at about 390, above the Results mean of 336.5 on day 17; both are series-level and no patient fact depends on them.
